claim_traces.claim_title: Humans only use 10% of their brains
claim_traces.claim_text: "Humans only use 10% of their brain capacity — the other 90% remains dormant and untapped."
reasoning_steps: The claim that humans only use 10% of their brain is a well-documented and widely debunked myth

Modern neuroscience, utilizing neuroimaging technologies such as functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and positron emission tomography (PET), demonstrates that virtually all areas of the brain are active and have designated functions
Even during sleep or simple tasks, vast networks across the entire brain remain active, and there is no 90% portion that sits dormant or untapped
Furthermore, evolutionary biology and clinical neurology show that unused brain tissue naturally atrophies or degrades, meaning an unused 90% would not be maintained by the body.

claim_traces.claim_title: Great Wall of China visible from space
claim_traces.claim_text: "The Great Wall of China is the only man-made structure visible from space with the naked eye."
reasoning_steps: The claim that the Great Wall of China is visible from space with the naked eye—let alone the only man-made structure visible—is a well-documented myth

According to NASA and accounts from astronauts, the Great Wall is virtually impossible to see from low Earth orbit without magnification because it is only a few meters wide and constructed from materials that blend into the surrounding terrain
Conversely, other human-made structures, such as major highways, airport runways, large dams, and cities lit at night, are far more readily visible from orbit.
